claims.statement: TFI registers Vault, Metrics, Workspaces, Assistant and Settings once through MobileFeatureRegistry, rejects duplicate IDs, and renders one NavigationStack per registration inside a sidebar-adaptable TabView.

MobileSceneModel owns scene-local routes, workspace selection and Assistant library over shared application services; Host activation reuses a recent matching terminal workspace in the scene's window session, while explicit connection actions can create independent workspaces.

Cross-tab selection stages a workspace ID until the Workspaces destination yields and pushes its detail; a dormant descriptor publishes a runtime within its owning window session before connection, and detail identity follows the selected workspace.

MobileContentRegions computes a largest continuous obstacle-free rectangle and an optional usable pair around an active division, retaining overlapping candidates; occlusions alone do not create a split.

Reserved-region and vertical-toolbar system queries are gated by both TERMIND_HAS_IOS_27_1_SDK and iOS runtime availability, with injectable test regions and fallback behavior; compact/regular layout is only a separate size-class hint.

MobilePaneLayout retains valid child sizes without replacing native surfaces; workspace content uses a continuous region while Assistant uses transcript/interaction regions, and both separately gate hidden hit testing and accessibility.
Mobile workspace switcher style and tab visibility follow toolbar placement, while SSH, Telnet and SFTP have distinct toolbar actions and per-action connection/capability gates.
MobileTerminalSurface owns its native terminal beyond SwiftUI navigation; added Find commands preserve ordinary terminal key handling and intercept Escape only while Find is presented.

Workspace-view disappearance disables Open With and window drop presentation, unbinds terminal upload callbacks, clears upload/drop targets and cancels drop loading without closing the runtime; drop handling requires a visible active detail and loading is cancelled on upload destination or connection-generation changes. Session close separately closes and removes the workspace.

Mobile Assistant shares application-owned execution/store services while scene libraries select conversations; focus restoration after replacement revalidates conversation identity, and the view composes an incremental native transcript with a measured scrolling interaction region.

TFI aggregates scene phases before entering background handling; background expiry suspends workspaces, stops forwarding, pauses transfers and expires Assistant work, while an active scene refreshes the current device name, resumes retained workspaces and restarts appropriate services.

MobileAdaptiveLayoutTests validates five native destinations across widths/languages/Dynamic Type and retained native list, focus and marked-text identity through injected region changes, rather than proving behavior on every physical device.
Mobile card columns derive from measured width, with accessibility Dynamic Type forcing one column instead of a fixed phone/tablet count.

TFI Workspaces Recents uses only local-device events and aggregates to five Hosts, Home Screen quick actions publish at most three host-only items, and the Vault History page presents at most 50 all-device events.

TFI renders saved and live Workspaces in one ordered 36-point Host-icon list with common title, address, protocol and lifecycle actions; connected live runtimes show a green eight-point dot, busy or reconnecting runtimes an orange dot, and disconnected/dormant rows no connection dot. Local Recents replaces the Workspace section only when no descriptors remain.

The TFI Workspace switch menu receives every ordered saved/live descriptor, marks the selected descriptor with a checkmark, uses protocol symbols for all other entries, and can select a dormant saved descriptor through the same scene route as a live Workspace.

Each MobileWorkspaceSessionModel maintains its own display order separately from live-runtime order: saved descriptors seed it, new and temporary workspaces append once, reopening a dormant descriptor does not move it, and closing removes its ID.

MobileAppModel rejects direct deletion of Tailscale-managed Hosts. Ordinary Host deletion closes saved and live rows across sessions, cancels related runtime work, then requests durable deletion; failures do not undo earlier cleanup.

Outbox handlers repeat Host cleanup; group deletion invokes ordinary per-Host deletion but excludes Tailscale-managed Hosts, and remote removal closes saved workspaces and clears connection history and Metrics selection.

UIKit-hosted adaptive tests check native tab identity and compact label visibility, retained navigation/edit sheets across resizing, independent scene presentations, adaptive switchers and in-flight save feedback; workspace restoration tests check that selecting a dormant row connects only it without reordering.

Vault owns navigation into Keychain, Port Forwarding, Snippets, Known Hosts and History; Vault search builds cross-feature links with forwarded query for item matches and routes Metrics matches to its separate top-level tab.

Vault History list actions belong to MobileConnectionHistoryView rather than the Vault landing page: it projects all-device events with a 50 matching-row cap and device-name search, shows disabled-protocol events without opening them, deletes individual events, and clears the entire history after confirmation.
Vault Host cards activate the scene’s preferred terminal; context menus offer enabled protocols, editing and eligible Tailscale details, with duplication and deletion disabled for managed Hosts.

Vault Host sections preserve nested and empty groups; group collapse is persisted as device-local library presentation state rather than a synchronized Vault group edit, and search still finds Hosts in collapsed groups. Group deletion can ungroup retained Hosts or delete the tree's Hosts through the app deletion path.

MobileActionCard gives the entire shared minimum-height card surface the primary button action and puts secondary actions in its context menu; mobile card surfaces adapt glass or solid styling to iOS availability and transparency/contrast accessibility settings.
Mobile Host cards display at most two tags without changing standard card height; card and forwarding-card layout behavior is covered by measured-height tests.

MobileHostEditor keeps a Host and Host-custom credential draft local to the sheet, uses shared presentation sections with SSH/Telnet-specific controls, validates host, enabled protocols, ports, identities, proxies and environment before Save, and delegates durable Host and custom identity persistence to HostCustomIdentityDraft via the library.

MobileEditorSheet owns dirty-discard confirmation, async save progress, error feedback, interactive-dismiss prevention and in-flight task cancellation on disappearance rather than allowing a failed save to silently close the editor.

Vault's Known Hosts is a separate card editor for SSH host-key entries: card tap edits, a secondary action copies the fingerprint, confirmed deletion uses the known-host store, and saving validates through app.knownHosts; hashed entries do not expose a recoverable port field.
Ordinary Host duplication creates an independent ID and removes Host-custom identity references; Tailscale-managed Hosts cannot be duplicated.

Workspaces Recents filters local events into a maximum of five distinct Hosts only when no saved or live Workspace is listed, while quick actions publish up to three openable Hosts from the same local projection and re-resolve terminal capability on activation.

TermindIOSApp constructs one MobileAppModel before WindowGroup content; MobileStartupView creates a window-bound scene model only after receiving a persistent UIKit session ID, MobileRootView retains it as @State and publishes a focused scene value for commands, and model-construction failure displays a data-store error instead of feature navigation.

Cold launch restores workspace descriptors without starting sessions or replaying initial commands; missing Hosts are pruned, while corrupt or unsupported snapshots report restoration failure and remain untouched by subsequent mutations when no successful first session binding occurred.

Removing the final active scene starts a background allowance only if other tracked scenes remain backgrounded; removing the last tracked scene does not start one, and reactivation before allowance expiry leaves a healthy workspace connection intact.

Batch Startup keeps one pending selection in the initiating scene until picker dismissal; its window session then rechecks current protocol compatibility and creates independent ordered workspaces without changing another scene's workspace selection, and opening Connect cancels an unfinished batch.

A window session notifies MobileAppModel to record a library Host's connection-history attempt before publishing and connecting a newly opened runtime; closing ends that event, while external-link workspaces with no library Host do not record one.

Home Screen shortcuts derive from local recent Hosts even when workspaces exist; the scene delegate consumes a shortcut once, Connect opens its scene's picker, and historical Host shortcuts recheck current terminal capability and report unavailable if the Host cannot be opened.

MobileAssistantModel coalesces repository loads into a shared conversation store, with independent per-scene library selections and drafts; sends are guarded against suspension, unavailable states and failed authorization, and background expiration cancels all runs before waiting for them and closing agent connections.

Different UIKit windows can create independent workspace and terminal instances for the same Host; per-window rename, close and workspace cycling cannot operate on a different session's workspace, although application-wide services can aggregate live workspaces across sessions.

First window-session binding after cold launch consolidates legacy unassigned and previously window-associated descriptors into the first bound session and saves before exposing them to another window; a failed consolidation fences that launch's claim and reports an error.
Workspace links preserve workspace UUID and route to its owning native window session rather than creating a copy in the receiving window; missing or removed owners report unavailable.

A temporary UIKit scene disconnect does not discard its restorable workspace session; when its native session is genuinely missing, an active session accepts live objects and descriptors after saving the handoff without reconnecting, while explicit native discard removes that window's work including previously recovered work.

Native multiwindow workspace routing is covered by opt-in serialized integration tests requiring TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1 with parallel testing disabled; these exercise ownership, activity links, system reclaim and native destruction in actual UIKit windows.

The Workspaces tab unread badge counts completion notifications in its own window session while the app badge sums workspace unread counts across sessions plus unread notifications from unarchived Assistant conversations; an active visible terminal marks completions read, and manual unread state transfers with window recovery but is not persisted in a workspace descriptor.

A native notification tap enters MobileNotificationRouter through MobileAppModel's notification service; the router retains terminal, Assistant and transfer targets until an eligible scene is active, routes terminal taps to the existing live workspace in its owning window rather than reconnecting or copying it, and requests native owner-window activation when a different window is active.

Assistant notification routing prefers a scene showing the target conversation or holding its selection before an unrelated scene; it loads the shared conversation store before opening a chat and falls back to the conversation library for a missing ID. Transfer notifications open the selected scene's Workspaces Transfers destination without marking unread terminal output read.

MobileNotificationRouter coalesces native window activation per target route, ignores failure callbacks from superseded requests, lets a later tap to the same target kind replace the earlier pending target, and clears pending routes and cancels its Assistant load when stopped.

Notification focus suppression distinguishes active visible terminal workspaces, visible Assistant conversations even when multiple scenes are present, and SFTP transfers when a scene is not backgrounded; mobile menu labels embed an unread indicator in native menu images so the indicator disappears when the entry is marked read.

Mobile scene selection routes to a workspace detail, but workspace connection journey and pending authentication belong to the workspace runtime, so detail navigation does not itself own or cancel the connection.

The shared connection journey presentation renders purpose-specific header/status and endpoint/checkpoint route, with activity scrolling suppressed under Reduce Motion; mobile wraps it in an inline scrollable detail rather than a sheet.

Mobile connection journey content prioritizes logs, then security-key signing, keyboard-interactive challenge, SSH authentication, host-key confirmation, failure, reconnect status, and phase status; prompt/challenge IDs establish form identity and stale keyboard-interactive cancel is guarded.
Mobile journey logs can be copied to the pasteboard and accessibility-size layouts compress the header log control and stack failure actions; the header log toggle honors Reduce Motion.

The same inline journey is used by workspace, Metrics, and port forwarding details, but each caller supplies operation-specific actions: workspace cancel closes the workspace, Metrics cancel disables monitoring and dismisses, and forwarding cancel stops the rule and dismisses.

Metrics selection and monitoring live in the shared application model rather than MobileSceneModel; the Metrics card view edits shared server state and its temporary picker selection is committed on dismissal, with persistence errors surfaced and limit failures opening the Pro paywall.
Replacing selected Metrics Hosts preserves configured selections outside the editable selector and rejects newly selected Hosts without SSH before persisting and applying configuration.

Metrics detail shows its runtime-owned journey while authentication is required or the journey is presented, otherwise normal Metrics panels; it stops detail observation during the journey, starts it when showing panels, and removes it on disappearance without stopping the shared monitor.

Metrics status and processes keep stable pane children with hidden-pane interaction/accessibility gates; usable region splits or wide undivided geometry show both, otherwise a selected page shows one, and its page picker is suppressed during a journey or two-panel mode and adapts to vertical toolbars.

MobileMetricsJourneyTests runs as a serialized but not environment-gated key-window UIKit integration test, restores the previous key window, and checks that a sampler-driven keyboard-interactive Metrics challenge stays inline and survives navigation, resizing and large type without a second connection.

The entire MobileConnectionJourneyRenderingTests screenshot suite requires TERMIND_JOURNEY_SCREENSHOTS=1; forwarding rendering integration separately requires TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1 with parallel testing disabled.

Host duplication preserves non-custom identity references and the rest of the Host configuration; the current MobileVaultFeatureTests duplication fixture checks that case, but does not exercise the Host-custom identity stripping branch.

On successful model construction, mobile startup gates the feature shell on diagnosis consent; the window-bound root creates its scene model in a task and delays pending workspace activity routing until the scene is active.
The Metrics view starts the shared monitor idempotently on entry, while the app's scene lifecycle separately starts or pauses it; leaving the Metrics view does not own or shut down monitoring.
A workspace retains its native terminal view across navigation; the platform adapter adds F3 and Shift-F3 Find commands and replaces Escape equivalents only while Find is presented.
Command-W closes the active Workspace or requests native session destruction when no Workspace is active; UIKit discard owns cleanup and a rejected request preserves the session.

The list keys pushed workspace details with .id(workspace.id), tearing down the old detail's UIKit search presentation when switching workspaces; retained workspace queries and the workspace-owned native terminal are not recreated by replacing detail identity.

SSH and Telnet workspace terminals remain mounted beneath an opaque journey in a ZStack, with opacity, hit-testing and accessibility gates when journey, authentication or host-key presentation is needed; workspace chrome and search remain outside that changing content. SFTP browser and Metrics panels instead branch against the journey and do not have the same journey-time mount guarantee.

MobileWorkspaceSearchModifier binds SSH/Telnet query and presentation to TerminalFindController and Submit to previous-match navigation; the workspace performs Find actions through its terminal. Native dismissal uses restoringFocus: false, unlike default programmatic dismissal, and ending Find retains the query for subsequent presentation.

SFTP toolbar search binds only the workspace channel query with no model presentation binding; it filters loaded file names case-insensitively after hidden-file filtering and before sorting, and native search dismissal retains this query rather than issuing a remote search or clearing the filter.

The mobile toolbar search UIKit bridge attaches its UISearchController to the navigation item of the ancestor directly inside UINavigationController, captures and enables definesPresentationContext, and removes/restores its owned attachment on owner changes or dismantling only if the navigation item still holds its controller; placement is integratedButton on iOS 26 and inline earlier.

Toolbar search configuration defers synchronization to the main queue to avoid publishing UIKit delegate changes during SwiftUI updates, also synchronizes on attachment and appearance, and honors optional model presentation by activating the search responder. isDismissing fences text synchronization, reactivation, edits and Submit until UIKit didDismiss, preventing mid-dismissal reopening.

MobileTerminalInitialFocus requests terminal focus on appearance or readiness changes, not ordinary updates; workspace readiness requires visible detail, active scene, connected runtime and no journey.

MobileTerminalSearchIntegrationTests is serialized and gated by TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1, uses a temporary key window with restoration, and checks repeated native/programmatic Find dismissal and retained query, SFTP close/reopen, and search identity through journeys. Its simplified production-modifier fixture verifies SSH attached-terminal identity but not full production SFTP browser retention.

MobileWorkspaceMenuTests is serialized and gated by TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1 and restores its temporary key window; it verifies opened/dormant descriptor order in title and icon menus, unread Assistant menu image updates, and Close Others availability only for multiple closable workspaces with no detail Close All action.
